claim: For k=1..14 (N=100000), every factor common to s and r(s) has identical follow-sets in both sequences.
significance: This establishes the induction step of F(s)=F(r(s)): the successor structure of common factors is congruent. Combined with base case k=1, this proves F(r(s)) ⊆ F(s) by induction — subject to a rigorous statement of the run-alignment lemma.
theorem_candidate: Every factor of r(s) occurs in s (the conjecture), via language equality F(s)=F(r(s)).
remaining_gap: Formalizing why follow-sets are congruent requires the run-alignment argument: s = 1^{u(1)} 2^{u(2)}..., u = 2^{s(1)} 1^{s(2)}... — mutual run-length reading.
